title: Peg Leg Bates and jazz endings today
summary: Peg Leg Bates offered help when Johnson had money trouble; Johnson dislikes dragged-out endings in jazz today.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: said, quote, "He could get music to talk to him. When he started getting good he'd say, 'talk to me, talk to me, baby.'" Speaking about friends brought a rush of memories. He mentioned Pegleg Bates, who also lives up in our area. And he said this about Pegleg,"several years back Pegleg heard that I might be in financial trouble. That's all he heard. But he sent word down, 'I've got you covered.' He's the kind of friend you don't have to see everyday to know they really care. They did not have to know what the problem was or anymore about it and I really appreciate that kind of man."
Commenting on jazz today he said, "Well, jazz today, the endings get to be dragged out. I'm from the old-fashioned school of music and music should end when it's supposed to."
